methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Apis Cor is a seed-stage construction technology company that has raised $5.5M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by a limited comparables universe: one identified private peer (BotBuilt) and no public construction-tech benchmarks, reflecting the nascent state of automated housing construction as a commercial category.

Given data limitations, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($5.5M, rounded to $6M as a proxy for post-money value) as the baseline, a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-Series A step-ups yields an implied valuation of $14M. This method is the only quantitatively supportable approach available given the sparse comp set.

The triangulated valuation range is $12M to $16M, with a median of $14M. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the single private comparable and the applicability of standard stage-progression multiples to a frontier subsector where comparable transaction data remains sparse. Any valuation in this range carries material sensitivity to near-term capital deployment, technical validation, and market adoption evidence—factors that would typically be stress-tested against a denser peer set. Investors should treat this as a directional estimate pending access to additional transaction or operating-metric comparables in automated construction.
